text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE STRAITS TIMES:
- North Korean agents try to get to top defector in South Korean consulate in Beijing.
- President Bill Clinton bans federal funds for human clone research.
- Singapore welcomes President Nelson Mandela with hybrid orchid in his name.
- Researcher says he is able to make a baby chicken sing like a quail by transplanting brain parts from quail into chicken.
- Khoo Teck Puat's plans to sell his Boulevard Hotel hampered as Urban Redevelopment Authority rules any residential development on site will have to be smaller than approved earlier.
- Thailand Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh suspends three central bank officials over bungled bank probe.
- Creditors of Amcol Holdings subsidiary Sankei given interim payments.
THE BUSINESS TIMES:
- Thai financial regulators in talks with international agency Moody on country's debt position and put in remedial measures to avert credit downgrading.
- Mohamed Saleh Sulong, long-time partner of late Yahaya Ahmad, seen taking over as DRB-Hicom head.
- White House subpoenaed for all documents on 14 individuals and subsidiaries of Indonesian conglomerate Lippo Group.
- Transportation-based Comfort Group in final lap of securing another vehicle franchise.
- IPC Corp stock up five percent on news of sale of new shares for Singapore $39.6 million to South Korean conglomerate Sungwoo group.
- Malaysian property group Landmarks Bhd in talks with Malaysia's Economic Planning Unit to acquire half Malaysian high commissioner's residence site in Singapore.
- Listed Hotel Malaysia Ltd lowers asking price of Boulevard Hotel to Singapore $450 million.
- Listed Keppel Corp to bid for 49.4 million peso project to upgrade railway facilities linking Manila to northern Luzon.
- Yeop Hiap Seng Ltd will soft launch Tivoli Gardens today.
-- Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
